name: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Qutayba al-Dīnawarī
summary: Philologist and man of letters of Baghdad, judge of Dīnawar, pupil of Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī, author of Adab al-kātib, ʿUyūn al-akhbār, al-Maʿārif and the books on the rare words of the Qurʾān and ḥadīth.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls him a Kufan by birth, named al-Dīnawarī because he was judge of Dīnawar. He took from Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī and others, and Ibn Durustawayh took from him. He excelled in language, grammar and poetry.

His books are among the best known of the third/ninth century: Gharīb al-Qurʾān, Gharīb al-ḥadīth, Mushkil al-Qurʾān, Mushkil al-ḥadīth, Adab al-kātib, al-Maʿārif and ʿUyūn al-akhbār. Al-Zubaydī counts him with the lexicographers of Basra; he lived and taught in Baghdad, where he died in 276/889 (some say 270/884).
uncertain: The year of his death: 276/889 in most sources, 270/884 in others (Ibn al-Anbārī gives both).

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 272–274
